notes: See AS097 for all Pachacamac khipus. 1. This is one of several quipus acquired by the Museum in 1907 with provenance Pachacamac. For a list of them, see AS97. 2. By spacing, the quipu is separated into 45 groups of 5 pendants each. There is a larger space after every 3rd group and a still larger space between the 21st and 22nd groups and the 24th and 25th groups. Thus, the quipu is in 3 parts: part 1 is 7 sets of 3 groups each; part 2 is 1 set of 3 groups; and part 3 is 7 sets of 3 groups. 3. All groups in part 1 have the same color pattern: W(with a W subsidiary); LB (with an LB subsidiary); YG; YB; YB:0G. Groups in parts 2 and 3 have the same pattern for the first 3 pendant positions and then vary in one or both of the last 2 positions.
